x-purpose: #1847 (checkpoints A and B). The ONE hand-written source of the public network contract: the operations an independently hosted Deskilo may perform against another installation's CURRENT discovery surface, classified public / participant / management. `dart run tool/build_public_network_contract.dart` renders the external and internal OpenAPI documents and the Dart adapter; test/tool/public_network_contract_test.dart fails when a rendering drifts, a binding is not what the SQL grants, or an operation has no consumer and test. The catalogue grants nothing: SQL grants, RLS and the RPC bodies stay the authority. Only implemented operations are listed; later features add their own operation, consumer and tests together.

capabilities.operation_header: The server revalidates `x-deskilo-operation: <id>@<version>` before a participant mutation and refuses a version it does not support. An unlabelled request is a client from before negotiation and means the operation's `unlabelled` version.

lifecycle: Reserved for #1850's capability maturity and lifecycle metadata. This installation publishes none: the descriptor carries no `lifecycle`, and a client never infers a maturity from its absence. A lifecycle term a client does not understand, listed in its `must_understand`, makes that one operation unavailable, never the others.

surfaces.public: Anonymous discovery of deliberately published projections. The request carries the installation's publishable key only; a session bearer is never sent (a fresh client per origin behind OriginOnlyClient).
surfaces.participant: An authenticated account acting for itself on the target installation, through its own session there. Capability or build claims grant nothing.
surfaces.management: Workspace authority (the owner) authoring what the public surface shows. Native sessions only (mcp_require_native); never reachable anonymously. Internal documentation only.

semantics.absent: An omitted key and a JSON null are the same: absent. A required field that is absent refuses the record.
semantics.unknown_fields: A key a schema does not list is dropped by the adapter. That is how an additive optional field from a newer server is ignored, and why a private field that leaks into a response never reaches a screen.
semantics.must_understand: A schema with `must_understand` names the key under which a server lists terms the reader must understand. A listed term this version does not know refuses the whole record; it is never silently dropped.
semantics.invalid_values: A required field with a wrong type, an over-long text or an enum value this version does not know refuses the record. An optional field with such a value is dropped: optional fields are descriptive only.
semantics.time: Instants are RFC 3339 strings with an explicit offset (PostgREST answers UTC with +00:00). These operations publish no site-local time, so no site time zone is part of the projection.
semantics.money: These operations publish no amount. A currency is an ISO 4217 code. A future amount is integer minor units with its currency, never a float and never divided by 100 by convention.
semantics.pagination: Offset pages over a total order (the listed `order`, column.direction, ending in a unique key; nulls last). A full page means there may be more. Query-bound opaque cursors are not implemented yet.
semantics.input: A management input key the contract does not list is refused before sending, never silently discarded; the server refuses it again.
semantics.negotiation: Before a participant mutation the client reads the target's descriptor (anonymous) and takes the highest version both support, provided it understands every capability the operation `requires`. A server without a descriptor is the pre-negotiation baseline: it implements version 1 of every `baseline` operation. The server revalidates the header; a capability or version claim grants nothing.

DirectorySource.description: A registered public endpoint of another installation: its origin and its publishable key. Never a session, a secret key or a private listing copy.

PublicContact.description: An owner, or an administrator who opted into public visibility. user_id is an account reference published only so a participant can open a conversation; it grants nothing.

PublicWorkspaceDocument.description: The projection the owner approved for public display, plus the workspace name, currency, booking unit and consenting contacts. No invitation code, plan, occupancy, price, internal note or operator stamp.

PublicWorkspaceCard.description: One published workspace, as the anonymous table read returns it.

PublicationInput.description: What the owner may write. Exactly the keys save_workspace_public_page accepts; every value is a string.

PublicationDraft.description: The owner's own page as the editor reads it back, published or not. Management output: every field optional, an unsaved page is empty.

PublicationPage.description: Whether the page is published, and its draft.

PublicNetworkDescriptor.description: What an installation publishes about its public network interface: protocol, capabilities and the version of each external operation. Never configuration, build, schema level, flags or people.

DescriptorOperation.description: One external operation the installation implements, and the versions it accepts.

OperationLifecycle.description: The #1850 seam: maturity and lifecycle of one operation. No term is defined yet; a server listing one in must_understand makes the operation unavailable to this client.

operations.summary: Read the installation's public network descriptor: protocol, capabilities and the version of each external operation.
operations.absent: PGRST202 (no such function): the pre-negotiation baseline

operations.summary: List the other installations registered in this installation's public directory.
Search the published workspace cards of one installation by name or address.

filters.search_text: ilike %query% with % and _ escaped; omitted for a blank query

operations.summary: Read one published workspace card again, live: no row means it is no longer published.
The owner reads their workspace's public page, draft included.
The owner saves the public page and publishes or withdraws it; answers the public projection it produced.
operations.idempotency: replace: the same document and flag saved twice has one effect; last write wins, there is no expected-revision check yet
side_effects: sets the publicListings flag to the published value
publishes or deletes the public card

operations.summary: A signed-in account registers another installation's public endpoint in this directory, after an anonymous probe of that endpoint.
operations.idempotency: upsert by origin; an account updates only its own registration; at most 20 per account

operations.summary: A signed-in account asks to join a published workspace, through its own session on that workspace's installation; admission stays the ordinary approval flow.
operations.idempotency: as join_workspace: a pending or existing membership is not duplicated
side_effects: opens an ordinary membership request; never activates a membership
